---
title: "Solution to statistical test task"
code-line-numbers: false
---

## Get started

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggsignif)
library(ggpubr)
```

## Part 1: Compare two species

### 1. Create a smaller version of the data

```{r}
penguins_small <- penguins |>
  filter(species %in% c("Adelie", "Chinstrap"))
```

### 2. Plot the two species

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot(penguins_small, aes(x = species, y = flipper_len)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

The warning about 1 removed row comes from a missing value in `flipper_len`.

### 3. Check for normality

```{r}
adelie <- filter(penguins_small, species == "Adelie")$flipper_len
chinstrap <- filter(penguins_small, species == "Chinstrap")$flipper_len

shapiro.test(adelie)
shapiro.test(chinstrap)
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggqqplot(adelie)
ggqqplot(chinstrap)
```

Both Shapiro-Wilk tests give large p-values and the points in both QQ-plots follow the line. The flipper lengths of both species are roughly normally distributed.

### 4. Compare the means

```{r}
t.test(adelie, chinstrap)
```

Mean flipper length was 5.9 mm shorter in Adelie than in Chinstrap penguins (Welch's t-test, $t_{119.7}$ = -5.78, p < 0.001).

### 5. Add the test result to the plot

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot(penguins_small, aes(x = species, y = flipper_len)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_signif(
    comparisons = list(c("Adelie", "Chinstrap")),
    test = "t.test",
    map_signif_level = TRUE
  )
```

## Part 2: Compare all three species

### 1. Pairwise comparisons

```{r}
pairwise.t.test(
  penguins$flipper_len,
  penguins$species,
  pool.sd = FALSE
)
```

All three species differ in their mean flipper length (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001 for all pairs).

### 2. Plot with significance levels

**Typing the p-values by hand**

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, y = flipper_len)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_signif(
    comparisons = list(
      c("Adelie", "Chinstrap"),
      c("Adelie", "Gentoo"),
      c("Chinstrap", "Gentoo")
    ),
    annotations = c("p < 0.001", "p < 0.001", "p < 0.001"),
    step_increase = 0.1,
    tip_length = 0.02
  )
```

**Extracting the p-values automatically**

In the p-value matrix, the rows are Chinstrap and Gentoo and the columns are Adelie and Chinstrap:

```{r}
pairwise_results <- pairwise.t.test(
  penguins$flipper_len,
  penguins$species,
  pool.sd = FALSE
)
p <- pairwise_results$p.value
p

comparisons <- list(
  c("Adelie", "Chinstrap"),
  c("Adelie", "Gentoo"),
  c("Chinstrap", "Gentoo")
)
adjusted_p <- c(
  p["Chinstrap", "Adelie"],
  p["Gentoo", "Adelie"],
  p["Gentoo", "Chinstrap"]
)
p_labels <- paste("p =", format.pval(adjusted_p, digits = 2))
p_labels
```

Very small p-values are shown as "p = <2e-16". The bonus section at the end shows how to get "p < 0.001" instead.

```{r}
#| warning: false
penguins_boxplot <- ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, y = flipper_len)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_signif(
    comparisons = comparisons,
    annotations = p_labels,
    step_increase = 0.1,
    tip_length = 0.02
  )
penguins_boxplot
```

## For the fast ones

### Other plot types

Mean ± standard error:

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, y = flipper_len)) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = mean_se,
    geom = "errorbar",
    width = 0.15
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_signif(
    comparisons = comparisons,
    annotations = p_labels,
    step_increase = 0.1,
    tip_length = 0.02
  )
```

Barplot with error bars:

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, y = flipper_len)) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = mean_se,
    geom = "errorbar",
    width = 0.15
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "bar",
    fill = "grey70",
    width = 0.65
  ) +
  geom_signif(
    comparisons = comparisons,
    annotations = p_labels,
    step_increase = 0.3,
    tip_length = 0.02
  )
```

### Make the plot look nice

```{r}
#| warning: false
penguins_boxplot +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Flipper length (mm)") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 16),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90")
  )
```

### Wilcoxon rank-sum test

```{r}
wilcox.test(adelie, chinstrap)
```

The Wilcoxon test comes to the same conclusion: flipper length was smaller in Adelie than in Chinstrap penguins (median 190 vs. 196 mm; Wilcoxon rank-sum test, W = 2733.5, p < 0.001).

### Normality of Gentoo penguins

```{r}
#| warning: false
gentoo <- filter(penguins, species == "Gentoo")$flipper_len

shapiro.test(gentoo)
ggqqplot(gentoo)
```

The Shapiro-Wilk test gives a small p-value, but the QQ-plot shows only small deviations from the line. With 123 Gentoo penguins, the test detects even small deviations from normality. The t-test is fine here.

## Bonus: Many groups

With many groups, typing the comparisons by hand gets tedious. Instead, you can turn the p-value matrix into a table with one row per comparison:

```{r}
p_table <- pairwise_results$p.value |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "group1") |>
  pivot_longer(!group1, names_to = "group2", values_to = "p_adj") |>
  drop_na(p_adj) |>
  mutate(
    label = if_else(
      p_adj < 0.001,
      "p < 0.001",
      paste("p =", signif(p_adj, 2))
    )
  )
p_table
```

- `as_tibble(rownames = "group1")`: turns the matrix into a tibble and keeps the row names as a column
- `drop_na()`: removes the empty upper triangle of the matrix
- `if_else()`: shows "p < 0.001" for very small p-values

`map2()` combines `group2` and `group1` into the list of comparisons:

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, y = flipper_len)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_signif(
    comparisons = map2(p_table$group2, p_table$group1, c),
    annotations = p_table$label,
    step_increase = 0.1,
    tip_length = 0.02
  )
```
